summary: Rhexenor was a figure in the Phaeacian royal genealogy in Homer's Odyssey, a son of Nausithous and brother of King Alcinous. Apollo struck him down in his hall while he was still a bridegroom without a son, leaving only his daughter Arete — whom Alcinous married and honoured above all women on Scheria.

sections.heading: In the Odyssey
paragraphs: Homer introduces Rhexenor only through his daughter. When Odysseus enters the palace of Alcinous, he supplicates Arete as daughter of godlike Rhexenor — the queen whose father Apollo of the silver bow killed before he could beget a male heir.
Alcinous took Arete to wife and the people honour her like a goddess when she walks through the city.
